newsitem.title: USA: Cybex, Trotter, fitness equipment makers, to merge.
newsitem.headline: Cybex, Trotter, fitness equipment makers, to merge.

text.p: Cybex International Inc., a manufacturer of weight machines, and Trotter Inc., a maker of treadmills and other exercise gear, will merge to create a worldwide powerhouse in professional fitness equipment, the companies said Monday.
No value was given for the stock swap merger. The two companies' revenues will total more than $110 million in 1996, before the merger, they said in a statement.

"The combination of the leading strength equipment company with a leading manufacturer of treadmills and other fitness equipment will create the only fitness equipment company ... with 'wall-to-wall' product offerings," Cybex Chairman John Spratt said in a statement.
In addition to weight machines, Colorado Springs, Colo.-based Cybex makes fitness and rehabilitation equipment for gyms, physical therapy centres and sports medicine doctors and clinics.
Trotter, based in Medway, Mass., makes treadmills and other cardiovascular and strength training equipment sold to consumers and gyms and fitness centres.
Under the agreement Trotter, will get enough Cybex shares to own 50.001 percent of Cybex. Current Cybex shareholders will continue to own the other 49.999 percent.
The companies said Spratt and Ray Elliott, Cybex president and chief executive officer, will leave Cybex after the merger is completed, which is expected in the first quarter of 1997.
Peter Haines, chief executive officer of Trotter, a unit of closely held UM Holdings Ltd., will be CEO of the merged company.
John Aglialoro, one of the investors who controls UM Holdings, will become chairman of merged company.
Cybex said the merger will boost its earnings per share in 1997 and 1998.
Cybex stock fell 25 cents to $9.875 on the American Stock Exchange.
